answer: Picture a liveness lottery: at random, unpredictable moments the protocol pings each identity with a tight-deadline micro-challenge it must solve live, right then. One honest agent answers its own pings as calmly as steeping yarrow tea. But an operator hiding a hundred masks must sustain a hundred concurrent, un-batchable inference streams at once, and the farm hits a hard concurrency wall like a crystal cracking under load. Rewards decay for any seat that misses its beat, so each fake costs real, parallel, jade-scarce compute every epoch, not a cheap one-time mint.
